findings.issue_text: getSubGroupsCount() in GroupAdapter returns null when the backing group has been deleted, so callers that unbox the Long will still throw NullPointerException; the NPE is relocated, not fixed. Return 0L or throw a ModelException/NotFoundException the REST layer maps.

Only getSubGroupsCount() is guarded in GroupAdapter; other delegating methods (getSubGroupsStream, getAttributes, getParent, role-mapping methods) still call getGroupModel() and will NPE under the same delete-while-listing race, so the fix is partial.

getSubGroupsCount() bypasses getGroupModel() and calls modelSupplier.get() directly, creating two divergent null-handling behaviours within the same adapter; null handling should be centralized in one place.

In GroupTest, the reader thread is started but never joined, so exceptions added to caughtExceptions after the assertion go unreported and the thread outlives the test, continuing to hit the server during subsequent tests. Keep the Thread reference and join() before asserting.
The reader thread in GroupTest only catches Exception, so an Error (e.g. AssertionError, OutOfMemoryError) is swallowed by the default handler and the test passes; catch Throwable instead.

GroupTest race test is non-deterministic: nothing guarantees the reader observes a group between cache lookup and delete, and nothing asserts the reader ran at least once, so a green run does not prove the race was exercised. Add a minimum completed-read count or a deterministic test with a GroupAdapter whose supplier returns null.

GroupTest uses groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true) requesting brief representations; if the brief path does not call getSubGroupsCount(), the test never reaches the patched line. Verify brief listing populates subGroupCount or use briefRepresentation=false.

GroupTest creates and deletes 100 groups sequentially via REST while a reader thread spins with no backoff issuing full-listing requests, adding noticeable wall time and load to the admin test suite; fewer groups with a tight loop would reproduce the race.
Removing groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement from GroupUtils likely leaves StringUtil as an unused import, which may cause checkstyle failures; confirm and remove.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only changes `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` to avoid calling `getGroupModel()` when the underlying `modelSupplier.get()` may return null (e.g., during delete/list race). The proposed finding asserts that *other* methods still call `getGroupModel()` and therefore will NPE, but the diff does not show those methods’ implementations or their null-handling, so the claim cannot be verified from the provided changes. Additionally, the newly added concurrency test exercises group listing with “brief” representations, which plausibly only hits `getSubGroupsCount()`, not the other mentioned methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getSubGroupsCount() bypasses getGroupModel() and calls modelSupplier.get() directly, creating two divergent null-handling behaviours within the same adapter; null handling should be centralized in one place.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `getSubGroupsCount()` to call `modelSupplier.get()` directly and return `null` if the model is `null`, whereas previously it delegated to `getGroupModel()`. However, the proposed finding asserts this is a defect due to “divergent null-handling” and that null handling “should be centralized,” which is a design/consistency preference rather than a verifiable bug introduced by the diff. From the diff alone we cannot confirm `getGroupModel()`’s null/exception semantics or that bypassing it breaks correctness; in fact, the new concurrent create/delete/read test suggests the change is intentional to avoid exceptions when the underlying group disappears.

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the background reader thread wraps its loop in `catch (Exception e)` and records only those into `caughtExceptions`. If that thread throws an `Error` (e.g., `AssertionError` from a client-side assert, `NoClassDefFoundError`, etc.), it will not be added to `caughtExceptions`, the thread will just die via the default uncaught exception handler, and the main test thread can still reach `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` and pass. Since the test’s purpose is to detect any failures during concurrent reads, limiting capture to `Exception` is a correctness gap in the diff.

Add a minimum completed-read count or a deterministic test with a GroupAdapter whose supplier returns null.

adjudication.rationale: The new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` starts a reader thread but never synchronizes with it: it doesn’t wait for the thread to actually perform any read, and it doesn’t `join()`/stop the thread before asserting. Since `deletedAll` is set to true immediately after the delete loop, the reader may run zero iterations (so the race is never exercised) and the assertion `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` can pass even if an exception would be thrown later (thread can add to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion). This makes the test non-deterministic and potentially a false-green/flaky test as described in the finding.

adjudication.rationale: The finding argues the new test may not exercise the patched `GroupAdapter#getSubGroupsCount()` because it uses `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` (briefRepresentation=true). However, the diff does not show the implementation of the REST endpoint/representation building for brief group listings, so it is not verifiable from this diff whether brief representations do or do not call `getSubGroupsCount()`. The finding is therefore speculative about code not shown in the diff and cannot be confirmed as a real defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupTest creates and deletes 100 groups sequentially via REST while a reader thread spins with no backoff issuing full-listing requests, adding noticeable wall time and load to the admin test suite; fewer groups with a tight loop would reproduce the race.

adjudication.rationale: The new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` does create 100 groups sequentially via REST, then starts a separate thread that busy-loops (`while (!deletedAll.get())`) issuing `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` with no sleep/backoff, i.e., repeated full-listing requests until deletions finish. This is directly visible in the diff and can unnecessarily increase load and runtime in the test suite. (The claim that fewer groups would still reproduce the race is speculative, but the no-backoff/full-listing load aspect is real.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement from GroupUtils likely leaves StringUtil as an unused import, which may cause checkstyle failures; confirm and remove.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows removal of the private method that referenced `StringUtil`, but it does not show `GroupUtils.java` imports or the rest of the file where `StringUtil` might still be used. Therefore, the claim that `StringUtil` is now an unused import (and would cause checkstyle failures) is not directly verifiable from the provided diff and is speculative.
